benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Rose to about $113.54 on 30 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 2.5% on the day though about 1% below this site's 23 Oct reading, after UKMTO reported a tanker was hit by explosives attached by a small boat 25nm northeast of Khasab, Oman on 29 October, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army separately claimed mine strikes on three tankers and a fourth (unverified); Ras Tanura's damage and the Houthis' East-West pipeline/Riyadh airport claims from 26-27 Oct also remain unconfirmed. Week-ago is this site's 23 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier.

benchmarks.label: WTI

peak.note: EIA Cushing spot high via FRED.

benchmarks.note: Rose to about $104.19 on 30 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 2.1% on the day and about 3% w/w, tracking Brent on the new Hormuz tanker attack and Iran's mine claims. Week-ago is this site's 23 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier.

benchmarks.label: TTF gas

peak.note: New 2026 high, the first close above €100/MWh, surpassing the prior 97.93 set 28 Oct (Trading Economics).

benchmarks.note: Rose above €100/MWh for the first time this year to about €102.89 on 30 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 5% on the day and about 10% w/w, as tight European winter gas supply combined with the new Hormuz tanker attack to lift the LNG-exposed benchmark. Week-ago is this site's 23 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier. Pre-crisis €32.00 is derived from RTÉ's figure of +€14.52 to €46.52 on 2 March.

extra_sources.name: RTÉ — European gas prices surge by 46% after QatarEnergy move
AleaSoft — Winter 2026-2027 in Europe: gas at highs and reserves at lows

peak.note: New 2026 high, surpassing the prior 31.42 set 23 Oct (Trading Economics).

benchmarks.note: Eased slightly to $32.04 as of Trading Economics' 29 Oct print, down about 1% on the day but still up roughly 6.6% w/w, tracking the wider gas rally. Week-ago is this site's 22 Oct reading (the site's JKM read lags a day), 7 days before that print. Pre-crisis is the IMF Asia LNG February 2026 monthly average, not a JKM daily print.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Eased to about $2.90 on 30 Oct (Trading Economics), down roughly 1.7% on the day but still up about 6% w/w; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price stays largely insulated from the Hormuz and Red Sea turmoil.

note: Brent and WTI rose on 30 October after UKMTO reported a tanker was hit by explosives attached by a small boat in the Strait of Hormuz on 29 October, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards and army separately claimed mine strikes on three tankers and a fourth (unverified). TTF closed above €100/MWh for the first time this year on the same news plus tight European winter supply. Henry Hub eased but stays largely insulated from the Gulf turmoil. Ras Tanura's damage and the Houthis' 26-27 Oct claims remain unconfirmed.
